title: Hero -> Model B robustness input (synthetic, fail-closed)
description: Versioned, fail-closed draft 2020-12 contract for a synthetic robustness-shaped input that a Model B robustness consumer (#425) may read. The top-level required blocks are schema, source_kind, provenance, information_boundary and hero_entry, and additionalProperties is false on every object so an incomplete or unknown field fails closed instead of being silently enriched. Everything is synthetic: provenance pins synthetic_fixture=true and every consumption flag false, and information_boundary pins every flag false, so this document can never be read as evidence about a real #367 result, a VALIDATION/TEST hand, a Model A output, a Hero EV or a recommendation. hero_entry carries the Hero action and sizing together with the public EV/uncertainty envelope, the paired delta, the evaluation route/source label, the support verdict (including ood), the posterior references and the candidate alternatives; each of these is explicitly nullable when the synthetic fixture does not provide it (null means not evaluated, never zero).

provenance.description: Fail-closed provenance of the synthetic input. All four flags are pinned so the document cannot be read as real #367/#314 evidence and never consumes a VALIDATION or TEST hand.

information_boundary.description: Hard information boundary. Every required flag is pinned false; a document that tries to open the boundary (Hero EV, Model A, recommendation, future cards or unrevealed opponent hole cards) is invalid by construction.

route_as_predictive_target.description: Optional reinforcement of the route/source rule: hero_entry.route_source (and alternatives[].route_source) is a provenance label only and must never be used as a predictive target nor as an environment weight. When present it must be false.

hero_entry.description: The single Hero robustness entry. Public Hero-side identity (action, sizing, optional decision/context ids) is carried next to the already evaluated public EV envelope, the route/source provenance label, the declared support verdict and the candidate alternatives. Nullable fields (action, sizing, ev, uncertainty, paired_delta, route_source, support, posterior_refs, alternatives) are present but may be null when the synthetic fixture does not provide them; null always means unavailable, never zero, and consumers must fail closed on a null/absent support rather than invent a verdict.

decision_id.description: Optional public decision identity, when the synthetic fixture names the Hero decision.

context_id.description: Optional public context identity, when the synthetic fixture names the spot.

hero_position.description: Optional public Hero position (e.g. SB), when the synthetic fixture declares it.

action.description: Hero action at the decision point, or null when the synthetic fixture does not provide it.

sizing.description: Hero target total in bb for the decision action, or null when the action has no sizing (e.g. FOLD) or the fixture does not provide it.

ev.description: Public Hero EV of the entry in bb, or null when the synthetic fixture does not evaluate it. Null means not evaluated, never zero.

uncertainty.description: Monte-Carlo style uncertainty envelope for the Hero entry, kept separate from Model-B environment uncertainty, or null when not measured.

ci95.description: [low, high] 95% interval in bb with low <= high.

paired_delta.description: Paired delta of the Hero entry versus the best alternative of the comparison set, in bb, or null when no paired comparison exists.

route_source.description: Named evaluation route and provenance source the Hero values came through (e.g. the harness/provider route that produced the synthetic EV). A route/source is a provenance label only: information_boundary.route_as_predictive_target is false and it must never be used as a predictive target nor as an environment weight. Null when the fixture does not label it.

support.description: Declared support verdict for the Hero entry, or null when the synthetic fixture does not declare it. status uses the closed #425 vocabulary, tier is a support tier label and ood marks an out-of-distribution environment that cannot be tested.

status.description: The closed #425 status vocabulary. Consumers map it onto the #199 robust/sensitive/insufficiently_supported verdicts (see docs/model-b-hero-robustness-consumer.md).

tier.description: Support tier label backing the verdict (e.g. LOW / MEDIUM / HIGH / VERY_HIGH / UNKNOWN). A tier never upgrades an unsupported status.

posterior_refs.description: Opaque references to posterior records used by the synthetic fixture, or null when not computed.

alternatives.description: Candidate alternatives compared against the Hero entry, or null when the synthetic fixture does not carry a comparison set. Each alternative carries the same public action/sizing identity plus its own nullable EV envelope, route/source label, support verdict and posterior references.

sizing.description: Alternative target total in bb, or null when the alternative has no sizing or the fixture does not provide it.

ev.description: Public EV of the alternative in bb, or null when the synthetic fixture does not evaluate it. Null means not evaluated, never zero.

uncertainty.description: Monte-Carlo style uncertainty envelope for the alternative, or null when not measured.

ci95.description: [low, high] 95% interval in bb with low <= high.

paired_delta.description: Paired delta of this alternative versus the best alternative of the comparison set, in bb, or null when no paired comparison exists.

route_source.description: Named evaluation route and provenance source for the alternative's values; a provenance label only, never a predictive target. Null when the fixture does not label it.

support.description: Declared support verdict for the alternative, or null when the synthetic fixture does not declare it.

posterior_refs.description: Opaque references to posterior records used by the synthetic fixture, or null when not computed.
